text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Albania has been suspended indefinitely by FIFA, the world soccer's governing body, over the government's sacking of the country's soccer federation head. The paper laid the blame on State Secretary for Sports Marjeta Zace for the move.

- Azem Hajdari, the self-proclaimed leader of the Independent Trade Unions, has asked an International Monetary Fund delegation to secure the money invested by members of his union in alleged pyramid money schemes.
- Albanian President Sali Berisha has awarded Mother Theresa, born of Albanian parents as Gonxhe Bojaxhi, the country's top "Honour of the Nation" medal.
- Italian ambassador Paolo Foresti has warned his compatriots not to get involvoed in alleged pyramid schemes in Albania.
- Vehbi Alimuca, president and owner of the country's biggest concern Vefa Holding, says his firm will continue to run its money scheme which offers monthly interest at eight percent.
- Eight former Albanian senior communist officials were sentenced to up to 22 years in jail for ordering the deportation and internal exile of anti-communist dissidents.
- Heavy rainfall has caused flooding and power failures in several major Albanian cities, with Lezha in the north particularly badly hit.
- Czech writer Milan Kundera has been awarded Albania's top literary prize, Ismail Kadare, by the cultural foundation Velija.

- Aircraft belonging to a Hungarian company have been regularly transporting automatic weapons and ammunition out of Albania to an unknown destination, according to an Albanian officer who took part in the operation.
He said ships carrying automatic weapons had also left the western Albanian port of Durres.
